stances.claim: Retirement meant 'a change of tires to prepare for a new journey' -- far from exhausting, the post-SC work breathed new meaning into the author's seventies.
Independent directors check management and enforce corporate governance -- the independence and integrity expected of them are similar to those of jurists, making the transition natural.

The two donations -- one year of columnist income to newsboy scholars; half of SC retirement pay to FLP -- reflect the author's conviction that 'liberty and prosperity must go hand in hand, and one is useless without the other.'

notable_anecdotes: The APOStolate coinage: the author as grandfather to 10 grandchildren -- 'APO' meaning grandchild in Filipino, and 'apostolate' meaning mission -- a portmanteau that characterizes his grandparenting as a vocation.

The newspaper dealer who threw a party 50 years ago for newsboys of Cataluna Street when the author topped the 1960 bar examinations -- and the author now donating a year's income to educate newsboys like his former self.

Sandy Prieto-Romualdez doubling the author's Newsboys Foundation donation on the spot -- 'so twice the number of newsboys would get the opportunity to study and perhaps have a chance to be chief justice 50 years from now.'
The awkwardness of being honored while still alive -- 'What can I really do, except to humbly thank the donors for the undeserved honor.'

decision_framework_signals: Treat retirement as a change of tires, not an ending -- design a post-SC vocation that extends the same values

one_paragraph_summary: On New Year's Day 2012, Panganiban counts his blessings since retiring from the SC in December 2006, when he thought his workdays were over and he would just pursue his 'APOStolate' (from APO, grandchild, and apostolate, mission) tending 10 grandchildren. Instead, retirement meant 'a change of tires to prepare for a new journey' -- Marixi Prieto's Inquirer column invitation, followed by Henry Gozon and Jimmy Duavit's GMA Network board invitation, and then a cascade of blue-chip independent director appointments (Meralco, PLDT, Petron, Metrobank, First Philippine Holdings, Metro Pacific Investments, Tollways, BPI, Robinsons Land, Jollibee, Asian Terminals). He finds the role natural: independent directors check management and enforce corporate governance, the same independence and integrity expected of jurists. The San Beda Law Alumni named a moot court in his honor; the PDRCI named its arbitration center (at McKinley Hill, funded by Bert and Sylvia Lina) after him. The Inquirer published 'With Due Respect' -- a five-year column compilation by editor John Nery -- as a 75th-birthday gift. Acknowledging awkwardness at being honored while living, he responds with two donations: one year of Inquirer columnist income to the Newsboys Foundation (doubled by Sandy Prieto-Romualdez, inspired by the newspaper dealer who threw a party 50 years ago when he topped the 1960 bar); and half his SC retirement pay to the newly formed Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity (FLP), which will establish professorial chairs, scholarships, legal research, new curricula, seminars, and an arbitration center -- operationalizing his core philosophy: 'liberty and prosperity under the rule of law -- justice and jobs, freedom and food, democracy and development -- must go hand in hand, and one is useless without the other.'
